title: Count weights restored common-plot biomass shares in 24 Cedar Creek treatment-years in 2017-2022
abstract: We tested whether released species biomass means represent common-plot community composition in a warming and drought experiment. Their sums exceed one in all 24 treatment-years from 2017 to 2022, by 1.19 to 4.70 percent. SD and SE imply counts of seven, eight or nine in 294 positive summaries. Weighting each mean by its implied count divided by nine restores total closure and all 96 functional-group shares within 4.3e-8. Simple normalization instead lowers dominant grass share by 0.65 to 1.85 percentage points. Four descriptive warming contrasts keep their signs. This is an internal summary-data check, not an independent ecological replication or proof of missing observations. The reconstruction assumes zero contribution from excluded observations. Small moving harvest strips still limit biological absence claims. Code, aggregate checks, a figure, exact source hashes and external retrieval instructions support reproduction. Raw data stay external.
